To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
visualization design can be enriched by considering a rich, multi-channel approach that includes the visualization process itself, the development of tools/techniques and the generation of insights.

visualization design and analysis is enhanced when it is conducted via multiple channels of communication, where each channel is designed to engage a different group of stakeholders and where the channels are developed in parallel.
the use of multiple visualization channels can lead to a rich, non- sequential visualization process that can lead to deeper insights and increased impact.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of visualization as a means of engaging a wide range of stakeholders in a complex, multi-faceted policy debate.
how to design for the `long tail` of visualization.
the design of a visualization system to support the analysis of large datasets and the development of visualization techniques to support the analysis.

this rich, non- sequential approach to visualization design fosters serendipity and deepens insight.
the visualization of data can be a very effective way to communicate and share information and ideas with a wide variety of people, and can help to inform decision making.
we have been successful in our engagement with these channels and that the insights we have generated are of value to the transport sector, to the visualization community and to the public.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to use a rich multi-channel data visualization process to support a range of different users in gaining insight into cycling behavior and in turn to use this insight to influence policy.
the visualization process itself is a rich and valuable source of insight, and that it is important to design visualization tools to support this.
the visualization process is an iterative process of exploration and discovery that is best supported by the creation and development of multiple channels of communication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
visualization is not a single activity but rather a rich, complex, multi-channel process that requires careful design and curation.
we need to move beyond the traditional model of visualization design and development, where a single visualization is designed, developed and deployed.
the design process for visualization should be seen as a rich and multi-faceted activity that can benefit from a multi-channel approach.
